entries.heading: What is checked
entries.text: The evaluator records whether a result came from running the protected task tests. A submitted score or a model’s claim of success is insufficient.

entries.heading: Who decides the outcome
entries.text: The model proposes a patch. The evaluator restores the trusted tests before running them, so edits to the model’s copy of the tests do not determine the result. Submitted patches are checked by the operators before…

entries.heading: What remains unknown
entries.text: Protected tests may still miss an incorrect or deliberately misleading solution. The rate at which such solutions pass has not yet been measured. Checks that a run followed the evaluation procedure cannot establish that…

entries.heading: Get started
entries.text: Quickstart explains installation and current availability. If you have access to the evaluation environment, continue to Run a task .

entries.heading: Explore the tasks
entries.text: Browse the task catalogue , then read about task packages . To evaluate your own agent, see Agent integration .

entries.heading: Understand the results
entries.text: The evaluation methods explain success rates, capability categories, and uncertainty. Quality summary helps you assess a set of tasks. Submit results describes how contributions are checked.

entries.heading: Use comparable evaluations
entries.text: The command needs at least one task and two models. Reference-solution runs are excluded. Use consistent agent settings and check task coverage before interpreting the summary.

entries.text: The summary reports discrimination, difficulty coverage, consistency, information, and reliability. Its readiness assessment is guidance about the task set, not approval of a score. Evaluation methods explains each…

entries.text: Use a capability filter to compare performance on a particular kind of task. A task can belong to several categories, so category counts overlap. Labels describe the repair; they do not measure its difficulty. Labels…

entries.text: Use the current report to inspect published task coverage and quality. View the quality report . Its measurements are provisional and should be read within the scope of the reported evaluation.

entries.heading: Start with task outcomes
entries.text: The analysis organizes results by task and model: each row is a task, and each column is a model. A completed evaluation reports whether the task passed. Some analyses can also describe intermediate progress.

entries.text: Operator-validated results and contributor claims are recorded separately. A submission does not become a verified result by declaring that it passed. Submission checks explain the distinction.

entries.heading: Information
entries.text: The information estimate combines how difficult a task is with how well its outcomes distinguish models. Tasks that are too easy or too hard for the evaluated models usually contribute little. More information can…

entries.heading: How it is estimated
entries.text: Task difficulty and discrimination are approximated from observed success rates and their relationship to total scores. The resulting estimate depends on this group of models and tasks; it is not an intrinsic property…

entries.heading: Reliability
entries.text: KR-20 measures internal consistency for tasks with pass-or-fail outcomes. It asks whether the tasks support a reasonably consistent total score across the evaluated models.

entries.heading: Read reliability with care
entries.text: Reliability is unavailable with fewer than two tasks or when all models have the same total score. A negative value indicates inconsistent task outcomes. Values around 0.7 or higher are a common rule of thumb, not a…

entries.heading: Confidence intervals

entries.heading: Tasks needed for greater precision
entries.text: The report estimates how many similar tasks would narrow an interval to a chosen target. The approximation assumes uncertainty decreases with the square root of the number of tasks. Treat the estimate as planning…

entries.heading: Tasks needed for greater reliability
entries.text: A second estimate projects the task count needed to reach a target reliability, assuming new tasks behave like the current ones. It is unavailable when the current reliability cannot support that projection. More tasks…

entries.heading: Signs of a weak comparison
entries.text: Most tasks are passed by everyone or by no one. Tasks cluster in one difficulty band or repeat similar repairs. Outcomes are inconsistent across tasks. Intervals are too wide to support a precise conclusion.

entries.heading: Default assessment
entries.text: The default assessment asks for a discrimination rate of at least 0.4, reliability of at least 0.7, and a discrimination interval whose half-width is at most 0.15. All three conditions must be met; an unavailable…

entries.heading: Limits on conclusions
entries.text: Small task sets give coarse estimates and wide uncertainty intervals. High consistency is uninformative when the models are too similar to separate. Low reliability limits how confidently a total score can represent one…

entries.heading: What an evaluation does
entries.text: A model proposes a code change for a task. The evaluator applies it and runs protected tests. The result records whether those tests passed.

entries.heading: Requirements
entries.text: Python 3.11 or later. For model calls, an OpenAI-compatible API endpoint and its credentials. For scoring, an Apptainer or Singularity host and access to the required evaluation environment.

entries.heading: Current availability
entries.text: The required evaluation environment includes unpublished changes to Harbor, the task runner. The public commands cannot yet score a task end to end without it. Installing the standard Harbor package does not provide…

entries.text: Use the project’s adapter interface and single-request example as the implementation reference.

entries.heading: Respect the evaluation boundary
entries.text: The agent must not read or modify protected tests or the reference solution, and must not assign a score. If it cannot produce a patch, report the failure.

entries.heading: Built-in baseline
entries.text: The baseline asks for one patch using the task description and relevant source files selected from the reference repair. It measures performance with those files supplied, not an agent’s ability to find them…

entries.heading: Agents with multiple steps
entries.text: The project includes an unfinished integration for agents that take multiple steps. It must be connected to your agent before use; its presence does not mean the agent is supported out of the box.

entries.heading: Make the configuration identifiable
entries.text: Give the integration a distinct name and version, and register it with the adapter registry . Report the same configuration details with every result.

entries.heading: What to submit
entries.text: Provide the proposed code patch, the task it addresses, and the model and agent configuration that produced it. Keep the original run record for reference.

entries.heading: How a result is checked
entries.text: Operators apply the submitted patch and run the protected tests in the required environment. They use that test outcome to determine the result. A claimed score does not establish a verified score.

entries.heading: After submission
entries.text: A recorded submission is pending until the operators evaluate it. The public release does not include an operational verification service, so recording a patch alone does not produce a verified result.

entries.text: The evaluation date and your contributor identity. The model name and the exact model release or build. The agent used and its exact version. The task identifier and proposed patch. Prepare a submission explains how to…

entries.heading: Validation
entries.text: Operators check the task, patch, model, and evaluation conditions together. Ranking also requires evaluated results for the complete published task set; a few selected tasks are insufficient. These checks are separate…

entries.heading: View submissions
entries.text: The submission page keeps pending contributions separate from verified results. Follow the contribution instructions when preparing a package.

entries.heading: Check the submission file
entries.text: Prepare a submission file using the contribution instructions . From the project checkout, validate its structure before sharing it. Validate a submission

entries.heading: Include the full evaluation details
entries.text: Identify the task, model release, agent version, evaluation date, and contributor, and include the proposed code patch. Keep these details consistent with the run you are reporting. Validation checks the file format…

entries.heading: Keep submissions comparable
entries.text: Use one model and agent configuration across the complete task set for a reported evaluation. Partial, duplicate, or mixed-date submissions do not establish a complete result. A corrected patch needs to be evaluated…

entries.heading: Use consistent conditions
entries.text: Operators evaluate a submission against a specified task set and evaluation environment. A result must identify those conditions before it can support a comparison.

entries.heading: Check the task environment
entries.text: The evaluator checks that the task image and runtime match the required environment. Unexpected changes stop verification rather than producing an accepted score.

entries.heading: Check the evaluator
entries.text: The task runner is checked before and after execution so a result cannot silently come from a different evaluator.

entries.heading: Read the actual result
entries.text: The published outcome must come from the protected test run for the submitted patch. A replacement result file or a contributor’s claimed score is insufficient.

entries.heading: Verify network restrictions
entries.text: For offline tasks, operators check that the environment can reach the network normally and cannot reach it during isolated evaluation. An inconclusive check is an infrastructure problem, not a failed task.

entries.heading: Separate checking from publication
entries.text: The systems that evaluate results and publish accepted results have separate permissions. Contributors cannot approve their own submissions.

entries.text: Each task includes a Dockerfile describing the source checkout and dependencies used for evaluation. Build from that recipe to reproduce the intended environment. Build instructions .

entries.heading: Reference solution
entries.text: Archived tasks include the repair from the merged pull request and a script that applies it. Running this solution checks that the task environment can reproduce a passing result. Live tasks withhold it.

entries.heading: Source information
entries.text: Source metadata identifies the repository, source revision, and license information. Tasks are drawn from permissively licensed repositories. This information helps readers trace a task to its origin.

entries.text: A live package lists the tests associated with the repair. Their names help describe the task; the protected assertions are withheld. A test name alone is not enough to reproduce or verify a score.
